runs.text: and then there are thought systems.
Most people never meet the architect.
Nothing is sacred except pattern integrity.
I used to think anxiety was malfunctioning.
It’s unconfirmed data with aggressive delivery.
I have a room in my head where ideas go to be interrogated.

pieces.title: What Success Looks Like In My House

runs.text: Success did not arrive with ribbons and bows. It came in small, repeatable proofs I could stack on a shelf and point to when the room got loud.
It looked like keys on a ring. Keys to offices that trusted me. Keys to homes I helped list and close. Keys to a life I built without asking permission.

It sounded like spreadsheets clicking into place. Cells that once fought each other now balancing to the penny. Closed ledgers reconciled with systems that never met. Work that would have broken me at fourteen becoming the kind of puzzle I finish before lunch.

It smelled like coffee at 5 a.m. and the inside of a car cooled by stubborn air conditioning on a Texas afternoon. It tasted like ordinary dinners that did not end in drama. Success is the luxury of boring. The luxury of a Tuesday that stays a Tuesday.

It looked like my kid laughing from the next room while I shipped something imperfect and on time. It looked like me on a stage with friends, a cheap mic turning into a good night, a song landing the way we hoped. It looked like a website that loads fast. A plan written in plain words. A client who calls back.

It felt like proof. Proof that I could pick up a shredded story and stitch it into function. Proof that I could walk into rooms that used to decide things for me and set the agenda. Proof that I do not need applause to be sure. I keep my own receipts.
I do not chase meteors. I choose bricks. The wall grows. People lean on it. That is success in my house.

pieces.title: The Woman Who Never Left That Town

runs.text: She texts her husband to pick up lemons,
she’s sorry she didn’t kiss him this morning.
She doesn’t know you’re dreaming of her.
And she wouldn’t believe you if you said it.

pieces.title: The Version of Me That Didn’t Say Yes

runs.text: She never Googles symptoms or replays arguments
She doesn’t know what she missed.
I don’t know what I kept.

pieces.title: Craigslist Ad from a Parallel Universe

runs.text: with low drama tolerance and a broken absurdity meter.
Arguing about font choices at 2 a.m.
Reading Yelp reviews out loud in a fake accent
Imaginary escape plans from small towns
Picking out strangers’ backstories at gas stations
Anything described as “a vibe” but not defined further
Must not cry when I speak plainly.
Must not rearrange my furniture, literal or psychological, without asking.
One loyal coconspirator, fully house trained.
